policy.rule: External claims are reference targets only unless DI runs the same dataset, grader, product configuration, and metric definition. Nearby DI metrics must be labeled as different tasks when those conditions are not met.

claim.summary: Augment reports 30–80% quality improvement when its Context Engine MCP is added to leading coding agents.

references.nearestDiDimension: T3 semantic question quality, correction burden, tool-call reduction
references.comparabilityReason: Augment measures end-to-end PR task quality with model/agent graders; DI's current benchmark measures deterministic repository intelligence and semantic retrieval.

claim.summary: Augment reports 65% precision, 55% recall, and 59% F-score on its public AI code-review benchmark.

references.comparabilityReason: The tasks and labels differ: bug-review comments versus evidence-derived semantic concepts.

claim.summary: Greptile reports an 82% bug-catch rate on 50 real-world bugs across five public repositories.

references.comparabilityReason: DI does not currently run Greptile's 50-bug PR-review protocol and therefore must not turn semantic/audit metrics into a bug-catch claim.

claim.summary: CursorBench 4.0 reports a current top score of 57.8% for ambiguous multi-file tasks from real Cursor sessions.

references.nearestDiDimension: multi-file natural-language investigation and tool-call count
references.comparabilityReason: CursorBench grades end-to-end coding-agent outcomes on private real-session tasks; DI's repository-intelligence probes are not that task set.

claim.summary: Sourcegraph recommends measuring retrieval, agent task performance, and cost separately and warns that a public benchmark cannot determine performance on every codebase.

references.comparabilityReason: This is methodological guidance rather than a numeric performance result.
